copy.title: The Gates Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Bill Gates’s family: who owns what, which stocks you can buy, the homes, the foundation and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #010 · The Gates family · Data as of
copy.h1: He plans to give it all away by 2045. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what each of them owns, which of their companies you can buy stock in, the homes, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file: what they own, what’s on the record, and where every fact comes from. The Gates children appear by name only.
copy.investLede: Microsoft trades on the Nasdaq. Bill’s private firm, Cascade, also holds big stakes in companies you can buy: Republic Services, Deere and Canadian National. Four Seasons and Cascade itself are private.
copy.moneyLede: The fortune started as Microsoft stock. He now owns less than 1% of Microsoft and plans to give nearly all his money away through the foundation by 2045.
copy.homesLede: The Medina house near Seattle, plus homes in California and Florida horse country. Prices are as reported. No street addresses here.
copy.recordLede: The money that shows up in foundation reports, tax and SEC filings, and the divorce. Filings and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From a two-man software company in 1975 to a plan to give it all away by 2045.

people.name: Bill Gates

summary.t: Started Microsoft with Paul Allen in 1975 and ran it as CEO until 2000. Now chairs the Gates Foundation. His private investment firm, Cascade, holds his stakes in other companies.

owns.t: Kept 44.9% when Microsoft went public in 1986. After he gave Microsoft shares worth billions to the foundation’s trust in 2022, Forbes estimates his stake is less than 1%.
His private investment firm in Kirkland, Washington. Bloomberg reported in 2021 that it held about $57 billion in public stocks and controlled about 270,000 acres of U.S. farmland.
Forbes valued the stake at $14.8 billion in November 2022. Cascade reports as a 10%-plus owner and bought more shares in August 2026, per Form 4 filings.
Forbes valued the stake at $7.7 billion in November 2022.
Cascade owns 71.25% after buying half of Kingdom Holding’s stake for $2.21 billion in a deal announced in 2021. Forbes valued his share at $6.6 billion in 2022.
Cascade sold about $940 million of shares in April and May 2022, leaving a stake of about 9%, Bloomberg reported.
Nuclear company he founded. It is building a sodium-cooled reactor in Kemmerer, Wyoming.

record.t: Has given more than $63.9 billion to the Gates Foundation, Forbes says. The trust that funds it held $92 billion on June 30, 2026 (unaudited).
In May 2025 he said he would give away virtually all his wealth through the foundation. It will spend more than $200 billion and close on December 31, 2045.
Announced May 3, 2021 and final on August 2, 2021. Bloomberg reported that Cascade moved stock worth more than $3 billion to Melinda by June 2021.
The Land Report named him America’s largest farmland owner in 2020, with more than 260,000 acres. Its 2026 list puts his land at 275,000 acres.

facts.t: Became a paper billionaire in 1986. Within a decade his net worth reached the tens of billions.
Bought the Codex Leicester, Leonardo da Vinci’s scientific writings, for $30.8 million at auction in 1994.
Paid $2 million for the Medina land in 1988 and about $63 million to build the house.

people.note: Bill has two sisters. They are private people and aren’t shown here.

kidsNote.t: Bill and Melinda have three children: Jennifer, Rory and Phoebe.

summary.t: Former Microsoft manager who co-chaired the Gates Foundation until June 2024. Runs Pivotal Ventures, which she founded in 2015 to work on problems facing U.S. women and families.

owns.t: Her investing, advocacy and philanthropy firm, founded in 2015.
Cascade moved about $1.8 billion of Canadian National and AutoNation shares to her in May 2021, Bloomberg reported.

record.t: Forbes estimates her settlement from the 2021 divorce at $25 billion.
Resigned as co-chair on May 13, 2024, effective June 7. Under her agreement with Bill, she gets $12.5 billion for her own work on women and families.
Bill gave $7.9 billion to Pivotal Philanthropies in October 2024, the first part of the $12.5 billion, per tax filings reported by Forbes.

facts.t: Joined Microsoft in 1987 as a product developer and worked on Encarta, Publisher and Word.
Announced in 2024 a $1 billion commitment through 2026 to women’s and girls’ rights.

people.name: Paula Hurd

summary.t: Philanthropist and former NCR executive. Her husband, Oracle CEO Mark Hurd, died in 2019. Bill confirmed they were dating in 2023 and called her his “serious girlfriend” on TODAY in February 2025.

people.kidsText: 2 daughters with the late Mark Hurd

summary.t: First woman to chair the national United Way’s executive committee and a University of Washington regent for 18 years. Also the first woman on the board of First Interstate Bank of Washington.

record.t: In 1980 she talked about her son’s company with IBM chairman John Opel. Soon after, IBM hired Microsoft to write the operating system for its first PC.

facts.t: Her grandfather, J. W. Maxwell, was president of Seattle’s National City Bank from 1911 to 1929.

summary.t: Seattle lawyer whose firm became part of K&L Gates. Co-chaired the Gates Foundation until he died in 2020.

record.t: Co-wrote Wealth and Our Commonwealth with Chuck Collins, a book defending the tax on large estates.

facts.t: Married Mary Maxwell in 1951. After she died in 1994, he married Mimi Gardner in 1996.

summary.t: Art historian. Led the Yale University Art Gallery, then directed the Seattle Art Museum from 1994 to 2009. Married Bill Gates Sr. in 1996.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.t: Started in 1975 and public since 1986, when Bill kept 44.9%. Forbes estimates he now owns less than 1%.

companies.name: Republic Services
companies.t: Trash and recycling company. Forbes valued the Gates stake at $14.8 billion in 2022. Cascade bought more shares in August 2026.

companies.name: Deere & Co.
companies.t: Maker of John Deere farm equipment. Forbes valued the Gates stake at $7.7 billion in November 2022.

companies.name: Canadian National Railway
companies.who: Bill (via Cascade, about 9% in 2022) · Melinda (got shares in 2021)
companies.t: Canadian freight railroad, also listed in Toronto. Cascade sold about $940 million of shares in 2022, leaving about 9%, Bloomberg reported.

companies.name: Four Seasons
companies.t: Luxury hotel company. Cascade owns 71.25% and Kingdom Holding 23.75%. No public shares.

companies.name: Cascade Investment
companies.t: Bill’s private investment firm in Kirkland, Washington. It holds his stakes in public companies, hotels and farmland.
